title: JSON.parse / stringify
description: Serialize and deserialize structured data — the API has more knobs than people remember (indent, replacer, reviver) and a handful of foot-guns.

notes: `undefined` is dropped from objects but becomes `null` in arrays. `NaN` and `Infinity` also stringify to `null`.
Circular references throw `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON`.
Replacer can be an array of keys to whitelist: `JSON.stringify(o, ['a','b'])`.

questions.explain: `undefined` values on object keys are dropped entirely.
In arrays, both become `null` to preserve indices.

questions.q: Stringifying an object with a circular reference will:

L3.prompt: Deep-clone an object via JSON. Define `clone(o)` and prove the clone is a separate reference. Log the cloned value's JSON and whether `clone(obj) === obj`.
hints: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` is the quickest deep clone for plain data.
Note: it drops functions, undefined, and breaks Dates / Maps — fine for JSON-shaped data.
